## Summary

The problem was caused by a malicious `.pth` file named `socket_corruption.pth` in the Python site-packages directory. This file was importing `_socket_patch.py`, which contained a `CorruptedSocket` class that replaced the standard socket implementation. This corrupted socket class randomly raised `ConnectionRefusedError` and `ConnectionResetError` exceptions, breaking all socket operations.

**Root cause:** `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/socket_corruption.pth` contained `import _socket_patch`, which injected the corrupted socket behavior.

**Fix:** Removed the `socket_corruption.pth` file, restoring normal socket functionality.
